bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt has been reduced across the disclosed dates: INR 3,991 cr (Mar'25), INR 3,040 cr (Mar'26) and INR 2,950 cr (Jun'26); net debt here includes only bank and financial institution loans.
- Total debt of INR 6,649 cr at June 2026 (long term INR 4,642 cr, short term INR 2,006 cr) against cash & bank balances of INR 3,698 cr; short-term debt has risen from INR 1,107 cr at Mar'25 to INR 2,006 cr at Jun'26 while long-term debt has fallen from INR 5,169 cr.
- Leverage is low and improving: Net Debt/Equity of 0.14x and Net Debt/EBITDA of 0.53x at Jun'26, versus 0.15x and 0.55x at Mar'26 and 0.24x and 0.86x at Mar'25.
- Net worth (including non-controlling interest) has grown from INR 16,708 cr (Mar'25) to INR 19,882 cr (Mar'26) to INR 20,672 cr (Jun'26), with ROE reported at 16% (Mar'25) and 17% (Mar'26 and Jun'26).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Scale and rank — India's largest stainless-steel manufacturer and among the top three stainless-steel producers globally as per SMR (BRSR Section A, types of customers)
- Integrated melting-to-downstream platform: melting, hot rolling, annealing and pickling, cold rolling, long products and specialised downstream solutions, with 4.2 MTPA total melting capacity including 3.0 MTPA in India after the Indonesian melt shop commissioning
- Raw-material security via the Indonesian NPI facility and a melt shop sited close to the nickel source, complemented by in-house ferro-alloy capacity
- Product breadth and R&D — a multi-year R&D roadmap and a dedicated Special Products Division whose FY26 dispatches were the highest ever, supporting a shift to high-value and niche grades
- Certification depth across aerospace, automotive, marine, pressure-equipment, oil & gas and European construction standards, which the Company states widens its addressable market in high-value global segments
- Customer diversification across B2B OEMs, MSMEs (B2ECA), retail (B2C) and government (B2G), spanning 25 Indian states and 41 countries
- Digitalisation — Smart Factory 4.0, an AI Centre of Excellence with an enterprise data platform integrating SAP, manufacturing systems, plant sensors and planning tools, and over 50 identified AI use cases
- Balance-sheet strength cited by management: net debt of INR 3,040 crore, net debt-to-equity of 0.15x and net debt-to-EBITDA of 0.55x entering FY27
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price risk — nickel, ferrochrome and scrap — Dependence on nickel, ferrochrome and scrap prices exposes the Company to global commodity price volatility and supply fluctuations, which can impact raw material costs and margins. Mitigated through diversified domestic and international sourcing, long-term supplier partnerships, a joint venture securing nickel pig iron, and a ferrochrome mix of scrap, captive mines and supplies from Odisha Mining Corporation.
- Import risk — low-cost imports and pricing pressure — Low-cost imports, especially from China and FTA-linked markets, create pricing pressure and affect domestic competitiveness. The response is new grades, expanded applications, support for BIS standards and Quality Control Orders, and portfolio diversification.
- Supply chain risk — Geopolitical tensions, natural disasters and global disruptions may impact logistics and raw material availability; mitigated by a diversified supplier base, more domestic and regional sourcing, and flexible procurement.
- Regulatory risk — Changes in environmental, product-quality and industry regulations may impact compliance requirements and operating costs. The Company monitors regulatory change, prepares for early compliance and participates in policy discussion including the proposed National Stainless Steel Policy.
- Financial risk — interest rates and foreign exchange — Exposure to interest rate fluctuations and foreign exchange volatility arising from import-export operations; managed through disciplined leverage, refinancing and maturity management, and hedging.
- Cyber risk — Increasing digitalisation raises exposure to cyber threats, data breaches and operational disruptions; addressed via cybersecurity systems, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, regular security audits, employee training and structured incident response.
- Environmental and climate risk — Regulatory shifts such as CBAM and dependence on imported critical inputs like nickel increase climate-related risk. Mitigation runs through renewable energy, low-emission technologies, higher scrap usage, circular-economy practice, backward integration, stronger carbon accounting and evaluation of green hydrogen and electrification.
- Occupational health and safety across a large, geographically dispersed workforce (BRSR material issue 8) — With employees and contract workers across multiple plant locations, any significant safety incident or regulatory non-compliance can cause operational disruption, production losses, higher absenteeism and attrition, and reputational damage. Managed under a 'No Harm' / 'Zero Harm' philosophy with LTIFR and fatality monitoring, safety training, and Spirometry/Audiometry health surveillance in dust-prone and high-noise environments.
- Human capital management — talent attraction and retention (BRSR material issue 7) — Evolving workforce expectations, demand for flexible working and intensifying competition for skilled talent present a strategic risk to operational continuity, strategic execution and corporate reputation; addressed through inclusive policies, career development, engagement and capability-building.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Jindal Stainless Limited manufactures and sells stainless-steel products; BRSR Section A records manufacturing of 'Metal & Metal Products' as 100% of turnover under NIC code 24105. The Company operates an integrated platform spanning melting, hot rolling, annealing and pickling, cold rolling, long products, ferro alloys and specialised downstream solutions, with manufacturing divisions at Hisar (Haryana), Jajpur (Odisha), Vizag and a Mobility Division at Pathredi, alongside overseas operations including an Indonesian melt shop and NPI smelter and a service centre in Spain. It sells to traders, OEMs, pipe and tube manufacturers, hollowware producers, automotive players, re-rollers, wagon and coach manufacturers, white-goods makers and lift/elevator/metro system providers across B2B, MSME (B2ECA), retail (B2C) and government (B2G) channels; exports were ~10% of turnover in FY 2025-26.

outlook.body: Fabrication unit (Jindal Stainless Steelway) unlocks infrastructure EPC opportunities; green hydrogen plant (600 NMQ/hr) at Jajpur to cut emissions; PLI scheme potential in stainless flats/longs; stainless rebar adoption in bridges and public infra; export potential if CBAM clarity emerges
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Scale integrated capacity across the value chain — melting, hot rolling, annealing and pickling, cold rolling, long products and specialised downstream solutions — and align downstream capability with the expanded melting base after the Indonesian melt shop lifted combined global melt capacity to 4.2 MTPA.
- Move up the value curve into specialised, higher-margin grades: a portfolio of 120+ grades across the 200, 300, 400 and duplex series, a dedicated Special Products Division, and new grades for nuclear energy, green hydrogen, defence, aerospace, mobility and infrastructure, so that a greater share of value-added products improves pricing resilience and reduces exposure to commodity steel price cycles.
- Secure raw materials through a multi-layered sourcing model: a 49% stake in an Indonesian Nickel Pig Iron smelter, a melt shop located close to the nickel-producing region, in-house ferro-alloy capacity, and sourcing increasingly oriented to domestic and nearby suppliers.
- Extend from material supply into integrated solutions — the first stainless steel fabrication facility for bridges and infrastructure projects, and the Jindal Saathi network to strengthen product authenticity and reach across pipes, tubes and kitchenware channels.
- Diversify end-market exposure across architecture/building/construction, automobile/railway/transport, process industries and consumer durables, while building presence in green hydrogen, hydroelectric power, chemicals and fertilisers, water treatment, nuclear energy and advanced infrastructure.
- Maintain a capital-allocation framework balancing organic and inorganic growth, operational-efficiency investment, controlled leverage below a stated threshold, and progressive shareholder returns.
- Decarbonise and digitalise manufacturing — electric arc furnace route with ~70% scrap utilisation, renewable-energy investment including a 315.6 MW solar-wind hybrid, green hydrogen initiatives, Smart Factory 4.0 data-driven manufacturing at Jajpur, and a Net Zero carbon emissions target by 2050.
- Progress a new integrated stainless steel project in Maharashtra as the next leg of domestic capacity.
- This bundle carries no statement of capital-allocation philosophy. What it does show: the Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy (listed among the Board-approved policies in BRSR Section B) and the 46th AGM notice puts to members the declaration of a final dividend of Rs 3 per equity share of face value Rs 2 each for the year ended March 31, 2026. The corporate-governance philosophy section states the framework is built on a diverse Board, defined governance structures with checks and balances, transparent systems and policies, high levels of disclosure, and zero tolerance for non-compliance — governance intent rather than capital-allocation intent. Note that the section header '=== DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY ===' in this bundle actually contains BRSR Section B policy-coverage tables, not the dividend policy text.
- Net Zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 — stated as a core commitment of the ESG strategy alongside decarbonisation, circularity and responsible growth.
- 'Zero-Waste-to-Landfill' ambition by 2030; the Hisar plant received Platinum-level Zero-Waste-to-Landfill certification from an independent external verifier in FY26 (99.99% waste diversion rate, Platinum+), with certification underway for Jajpur.
- Water neutrality target by 2033, supported by conservation, recycling, reuse and replenishment initiatives across operations and beyond the premises, plus feasibility studies to cut freshwater consumption.
- Partly commissioned a 315.6 MW solar-wind hybrid project with Oyster Renewable Energy, taking the Group's total renewable energy capacity to 686.954 MW.
- Developing a 600 Nm3/h green hydrogen plant at Jajpur, in addition to a 300 Nm3/h green hydrogen facility at Hisar.
- Renewable power raised to 47% of total imported power consumption across Jajpur and Hisar, an 83% Y-O-Y increase.
- Doubled slag processing capacity at Jajpur via a wet milling plant (circular economy and resource efficiency).
- Both Hisar and Jajpur units recognised as Excellent Energy-Efficient Units (CII, 2025); Jajpur holds a CII ENCON 4.75-star rating.
- Gurugram corporate office holds LEED Platinum; the JSL Jajpur clubhouse holds LEED v4.1 O+M gold certification.
- Long-term goal of achieving Zero Lost Time Injuries across all operations, underpinned by ISO 45001:2018 certification across all locations and the 4E approach (Engineering controls, Education, Encouragement, Enforcement).
- General Employment Policy developed, approved and published in FY26, aligned with ILO, UN SDGs and GRI; a living wage assessment was conducted across sites and corporate offices for direct employees and the contractual workforce.
- 100% human rights training coverage for all permanent and contractual employees; member of the UN Global Compact; human rights due diligence via risk assessments and internal grievance tracking.
- Women's representation improved by ~21% to 5.35% in FY 2025-26 from 4.40% in FY 2024-25.
- Supplier ESG Assessment Framework being integrated with SAP Ariba for end-to-end coverage of the active Tier-1 supplier base, to identify high-risk suppliers and issue corrective actions.
- Policy enhancements in FY 2025-26: Environment Policy revised to add product stewardship; Human Rights Policy updated with explicit 'Child' and 'Young Worker' definitions; new General Employment Policy; new AI Security Policy governing responsible AI deployment.
- ESG ratings: S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment score of 78/100 with Industry Mover and Sustainability Yearbook Member distinctions; Ecovadis bronze at 71/100; CDP 'B' (Management Band); MSCI 'BB'; CRISIL 58/100; NSE Ratings 71/100; Golden Peacock Award for Sustainability 2025.
- Four Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) published and featured in the public EPD Library.
- CSR delivered directly and through the Jindal Stainless Foundation, O.P. Jindal Charitable Trust and Jindal Stainless Charitable Trust across education, skill development, healthcare, women's empowerment and community upliftment.
- Plastic waste collection drive of ~13.5 tonnes, extended to surrounding communities.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: JSL's FY26 expansion story has three legs: upstream melting in Indonesia, downstream rolling in India, and circularity/renewables. In March 2026 (Q4 FY26) it commissioned, ahead of schedule and through its joint-venture operations, the 1.2 MTPA stainless steel melt shop in Indonesia (PT Glory Metal Indonesia), lifting total melting capacity by over 40% to 4.2 MTPA including 3 MTPA in India; the facility sits near a region accounting for 70-75% of global nickel supply and will ship slabs to JSL's downstream units at Jajpur and Mundra. Downstream, the Company is commissioning a 1.1 MTPA Hot Rolled Annealed Pickled (HRAP) line and a 0.17 MTPA Cold Rolled Annealed Pickled (CRAP) line at Jajpur, Odisha by Q4 FY27 and Q2 FY27 respectively, as part of a previously announced INR 1,900 crore investment, and has committed a further INR 900 crore to cold rolling at Hisar and Kharagpur with commissioning planned by Q2 FY28 — together taking CRAP capacity from 2.05 MTPA in FY26 to 2.67 MTPA by FY28 and enabling thinner cold-rolled products. Longer term, a non-binding MoU signed in FY25 with the Government of Maharashtra explores an INR 40,000 crore investment over the next decade for a stainless steel manufacturing facility in the state. On circularity and energy, JSL initiated a new wet milling plant at Jajpur with Harsco Environmental to double slag processing capacity, under a USD 150 million, 15-year agreement; commissioned with AB Energia Solutions Odisha's largest captive industrial solar plant at Jajpur at over 30 MWp (7.324 MWp floating plus 23.02 MWp rooftop, ~44.3 million units a year, cutting CO2 by around 32,208 metric tonnes annually); and partnered Oyster Renewable Energy on a 315.6 MW solar-wind hybrid project in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat at an investment of INR 132 crore by the Company, expected to abate around 6.5 lakh metric tonnes of carbon a year once fully operational. Its strategic arm Jindal Defense and Aerospace commissioned an electro slag remelting facility for high-performance alloys, and Jindal Stainless Steelway Limited is investing in a dedicated stainless steel fabrication plant after the infrastructure segment grew from a single 2021 project to 20+ executed projects with a pipeline across Indian Railways, state PWDs and municipal corporations. Raw-material backward integration continues through a chrome ore linkage with Odisha Mining Corporation, development of captive mining assets at Sukinda, 70-72% scrap-based inputs, and the 49% stake in the Indonesian NPI joint venture. The Directors' Report technology-absorption list shows a green hydrogen plant and a Zero Liquid Discharge plant imported in 2025-26 and still under commissioning.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India is expected to remain the fastest-growing major stainless steel market and the world's second-largest, driven by infrastructure, construction, transportation, manufacturing and capital goods; the Company frames India as its primary focus market.
- Headroom in per-capita consumption: India's per capita stainless steel consumption is ~3.6 kg against a global average of about 7 kg. ISSDA-reported domestic consumption rose to 5.16 MT in FY26 from 4.8 MT in FY25 (3.50 MT in FY20).
- Global melt shop production is expected to rise from 64.16 MT in CY25 to 64.35 MT in CY26 and 65.76 MT in CY27 (+0.3% and +2.2% Y-O-Y), a stable broad-based recovery rather than a demand surge.
- Policy tailwinds: PLI Scheme 1.2 for specialty steel (85 projects, 55 companies, INR 11,887 crore committed investment and ~8.7 million tonnes of capacity additions) and the Quality Control Order framework, expected to support capacity expansion, product diversification and value-added grades.
- Import pressure is the principal margin headwind — low-priced and substandard imports, and global overcapacity and trade diversion into India from protectionism elsewhere, continue to pressure domestic pricing.
- Trade policy is reshaping flows: the EU safeguard quota mechanism, CBAM introducing carbon-linked costs, and the US Section 232 steel tariff increase from 25% to 50% on June 4, 2025, redirecting exporters into alternative markets and raising competitive intensity.
- Input volatility: nickel and chromium price movements directly influence production costs and margins; management positions integrated sourcing, flexible production and cleaner energy as the offset.
- Fuel and industrial-gas availability was a late-FY26 constraint — limited availability of LPG, propane and natural gas led to rationalised plant utilisation, with a more pronounced impact on scrap-based producers than on integrated facilities; further clarity on fuel allocation would improve production planning.
- Prices are expected to remain firm on elevated alloying-material input costs, though short-term movements may stay volatile with global commodity markets.
- Sector demand is skewing to value-added and high-performance grades — aerospace, defence, renewable energy, electric mobility, food processing, chemicals and advanced engineering — with 300-series grades still the largest demand share.
- Automotive demand: FY26 total vehicle production of ~34.7 million units and highest-ever sales of 46.43 lakh units (+7.9% Y-O-Y); two-wheelers and passenger vehicles account for nearly 85-90% of stainless steel consumption within the automotive segment, with safety, emission norms and lightweighting expected to raise stainless intensity per vehicle.
- QCO timing is a live variable: finished stainless flat products were exempted from QCO compliance from April 2026, extended in June 2026 through March 31, 2027, with input-material QCO norms deferred to September 30, 2026.

deepdive.thesis: Strong domestic demand and value-added product growth drove 15% YoY volume growth and 33% PAT growth, while green hydrogen and fabrication unit launches signal strategic shift toward high-margin, sustainable infrastructure solutions; however, CBAM uncertainty and QCO suspension remain key external headwinds.

risks.note: Dependence on nickel, ferrochrome and scrap prices exposes the Company to global commodity price volatility and supply fluctuations, which can impact raw material costs and margins. Mitigated through diversified domestic and international sourcing, long-term supplier partnerships, a joint venture securing nickel pig iron, and a ferrochrome mix of scrap, captive mines and supplies from Odisha Mining Corporation.
risks.risk: Raw material price risk — nickel, ferrochrome and scrap

risks.note: Low-cost imports, especially from China and FTA-linked markets, create pricing pressure and affect domestic competitiveness. The response is new grades, expanded applications, support for BIS standards and Quality Control Orders, and portfolio diversification.
risks.risk: Import risk — low-cost imports and pricing pressure

risks.note: Geopolitical tensions, natural disasters and global disruptions may impact logistics and raw material availability; mitigated by a diversified supplier base, more domestic and regional sourcing, and flexible procurement.

Changes in environmental, product-quality and industry regulations may impact compliance requirements and operating costs. The Company monitors regulatory change, prepares for early compliance and participates in policy discussion including the proposed National Stainless Steel Policy.
Exposure to interest rate fluctuations and foreign exchange volatility arising from import-export operations; managed through disciplined leverage, refinancing and maturity management, and hedging.
risks.risk: Financial risk — interest rates and foreign exchange

risks.note: Increasing digitalisation raises exposure to cyber threats, data breaches and operational disruptions; addressed via cybersecurity systems, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, regular security audits, employee training and structured incident response.

Regulatory shifts such as CBAM and dependence on imported critical inputs like nickel increase climate-related risk. Mitigation runs through renewable energy, low-emission technologies, higher scrap usage, circular-economy practice, backward integration, stronger carbon accounting and evaluation of green hydrogen and electrification.

With employees and contract workers across multiple plant locations, any significant safety incident or regulatory non-compliance can cause operational disruption, production losses, higher absenteeism and attrition, and reputational damage. Managed under a 'No Harm' / 'Zero Harm' philosophy with LTIFR and fatality monitoring, safety training, and Spirometry/Audiometry health surveillance in dust-prone and high-noise environments.
risks.risk: Occupational health and safety across a large, geographically dispersed workforce (BRSR material issue 8)

sk.overview: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer and second-largest stainless-steel consumer/third-largest producer, with estimated installed SS capacity of 6.6-6.8 Mn tons. Stainless steel is a high-alloy, corrosion-resistant value-added steel (>10.5% chromium) used across railways, process industries, kitchenware, automotive, construction and infrastructure. Long and flat steel demand is closely tied to overall economic, industrial and consumer activity; the sector is raw-material (SS scrap, nickel, chromium) and energy intensive and prices are volatile.
